explanation: The Christian apostle who was formerly known as Saul of Tarsus and now defended his conversion and calling before a Roman crowd.
A person who speaks on behalf of others, here used of Paul defending himself against accusations in Jerusalem.
A place where prisoners are held; Paul was captured and placed under Roman guard to prevent an uprising by the Jews.
The legal rights a Roman citizen possessed, including protection from unjust punishment and the right to appeal to the emperor.
A supernatural revelation or sight; Paul describes how the Lord Jesus appeared to him on the road to Damascus.
People who cannot hear, used here metaphorically of the Jews who were blind and deaf to God's message before being enlightened.
The voice Paul heard from heaven during his vision on the road to Damascus, which commanded him to go out among the Gentiles.
People who are not Jews; nations outside the chosen people of Israel, now included in God's plan of salvation through Paul's mission.
